2 Two lists per half: whitelist proved or enforced, blacklist recorded

5 Traceability half authored, half rendered; the status line its subset
6 Three template sections dissolve; a tag on every section

cards.title: Rules in force
items: ADR before intake; intake before any unit
One commit per unit; Developer then Verifier
Ready-green or parked, never half-ready
A Contract: trailer on every commit touching a non-free path
New context enters the document before the conversation

cards.title: Glossary
items: 0026: ADR, the feature document is the raw request; the contract is what intake produces from it
0028: ADR, the interview writes the feature document; /sdlc:product-specification-interview; ships in 0.13.0
0029: ADR, one format and a definition of done for the feature document; amends 0026's template changes
The line: the seat boundary in the document; the PO seat signs above, the engineer seat below
Check: a one-line acceptance criterion with an id (SC3.1) under a success criterion; the contract's acceptance_sketch; the Gherkin is derived from it
Derived block: the contract, the Gherkin, the traceability record; read-only, stamped with the revision it came from; stale when a newer row exists
Measured: row: a revision row that records a look at the real system; the newest is the last-measured date
Parked: a seat's answer is missing, a dependency is blocked, or an OPEN question stands; the contract validates as draft and waits
Two-Key: a unit is done only when the Verifier re-runs the tests independently and grades PASS
ready-green: the contract passes the ready validation profile; development starts only from green
Seat: a human role that answers at intake (PO, engineer), recorded per unit in confirmed_by
Contract: trailer: the binding of a commit to its contract; scope-check (G4.12) reads it; free paths pass without one
Self-pin: after a release, the kit's own workflow refs move to the new tag; the last act of every release
5b: proposed step, taskcontract graph emits Archify beside its Mermaid (0024); two units, its own contract, before the demo
F1-F6: the proposed units of the feature-document contract; V1-V6: wave B's
